# Answer: generator shortcuts

The strongest plausible rival is **“any intersecting third-color object blocks a candidate bridge.”** It differs from the intended rule only in blocker color: the canonical rule suppresses a bridge when a *same-color* third bounding box intersects the bridge rectangle; the rival suppresses it for a third box of any color. That rival matches all four canonical pairs, as checked in `checks/shortcut-witness/canonical-rival.json` (`all_rival_fit: true`).

An exact disagreement input is retained in `checks/shortcut-witness/input.json`. It is a production-lawful draw from final generator SHA-256 `e3465bcdcdcad8ad2bb616bc4301d69eb24a36b4bffbc7bce3dc771e5816cf04`, generated by `seed=17`, `sample_index=0`, `scene_profile="horizontal_pair"`; its `self_check` result is empty. The selected canonical Racket authority was executed with:

`python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply cfadc43e5098 --input ../checks/shortcut-witness/input.json --check-generator-domain --timeout 300 --out ../checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json`

The exact canonical Racket output is in `checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json`; the rival output and a combined, hash-bound comparison are in `checks/shortcut-witness/witness.json`. They differ in 40 cells: the canonical rule paints through the differently colored 3×3 obstacle, while the rival leaves that bridge unpainted.

The repaired generator deliberately emits this distinction. Every one of the eight general scene profiles now contains a differently colored box inside an unblocked bridge. The 12-profile interleaved schedule puts at least two general profiles in every cyclic four-pair lesson, so every three-demonstration holdout and every one-query rotation retains a refuter. Final evidence: `checks/lesson-census-final-3.summary.json` reports 0 ambiguous production lessons out of 300 and 0 ambiguous rotations out of 1,200; `checks/semantic-after-enumerated/` exhausts all 12 declared schedule starts at seed 0.
